questions.question:
Given that the inverse trigonometric function assumes principal values only. Let \(x\), \(y\) be any two real numbers in [-1,1] such that cos-1x-sin-1y=α,-π2≤α≤π. Then, the minimum value of x2+y2+2xysinα is

 

[JEE Main 2024, 4 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The condition is

\(\cos^{-1}x-\sin^{-1}y=\alpha\)

\(\Rightarrow \cos^{-1}x=\alpha+\sin^{-1}y\)

Taking cosine,

\(x=\cos\left(\alpha+\sin^{-1}y\right)\)

Since \(\cos(\sin^{-1}y)=\sqrt{1-y^2}\),

\(x=\cos\alpha\sqrt{1-y^2}-y\sin\alpha\)

\(\Rightarrow x+y\sin\alpha=\cos\alpha\sqrt{1-y^2}\)

Now \(x^2+y^2+2xy\sin\alpha=(x+y\sin\alpha)^2+y^2\cos^2\alpha\)

\(\Rightarrow x^2+y^2+2xy\sin\alpha=\cos^2\alpha(1-y^2)+y^2\cos^2\alpha\)

\(\Rightarrow x^2+y^2+2xy\sin\alpha=\cos^2\alpha\)

For \(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\leq\alpha\leq\pi\), the minimum value of \(\cos^2\alpha\) is \(0\), attained at \(\alpha=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\).

[JEE Main 2024, 4 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
We have

\(f(0)=0\), \(f(1)=1\), \(f(2)=-1\), \(f(3)=2\), and \(f(4)=-2\).

Since \(f(1)\) and \(f(2)\) have opposite signs, there is at least one number \(r_1\in(1,2)\)

such that \(f(r_1)=0\)

Since \(f(2)\) and \(f(3)\) have opposite signs, there is at least one number \(r_2\in(2,3)\)

such that \(f(r_2)=0\)

Since \(f(3)\) and \(f(4)\) have opposite signs, there is at least one number \(r_3\in(3,4)\)

such that \(f(r_3)=0\)

Thus, \(f\) has at least four distinct zeros:

\(0,r_1,r_2,r_3\).

By Rolle's theorem, there is at least one zero of \(f'\) in each of the intervals

\((0,r_1)\), \((r_1,r_2)\), and \((r_2,r_3)\).

Therefore, \(f'\) has at least three distinct zeros that are different from the four zeros of \(f\).

Let \(H(x)=f(x)f'(x)\).

At every zero of \(f\) or \(f'\), we have \(H(x)=0\).

Hence, \(H\) has at least \(4+3=7\) distinct zeros.

Applying Rolle's theorem once, \(H'\) has at least \(6\) zeros.

Applying Rolle's theorem again, \(H''\) has at least \(5\) zeros.

Now, \(H'(x)=(f'(x))^2+f(x)f''(x)\).

Differentiating again,

\(H''(x)=2f'(x)f''(x)+f'(x)f''(x)+f(x)f'''(x)\)

\(=3f'(x)f''(x)+f(x)f'''(x)\).

Therefore, the minimum guaranteed number of zeros of \((3f'f''+ff''')(x)\) is \(5\).

questions.question:
If ∫cosec5xdx=αcotxcosecxcosec2x+32+βlogetanx2+C where α,β∈R and C is the constant of integration, then the value of 8(α+β) equals ______.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 4 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(I=\int\operatorname{cosec}^5x\,dx\).

Write \(I=\int\operatorname{cosec}^3x\operatorname{cosec}^2x\,dx\).

Using integration by parts, take \(u=\operatorname{cosec}^3x\) and \(dv=\operatorname{cosec}^2x\,dx\).

Then \(du=-3\operatorname{cosec}^3x\cot x\,dx\) and \(v=-\cot x\).

Therefore, \(I=-\operatorname{cosec}^3x\cot x-3\int\operatorname{cosec}^3x\cot^2x\,dx\).

Using \(\cot^2x=\operatorname{cosec}^2x-1\), we get \(I=-\operatorname{cosec}^3x\cot x-3I+3\int\operatorname{cosec}^3x\,dx\).

Hence \(4I=-\operatorname{cosec}^3x\cot x+3J\), where \(J=\int\operatorname{cosec}^3x\,dx\).

For \(J\), write \(J=\int\operatorname{cosec}x\operatorname{cosec}^2x\,dx\).

Using integration by parts with \(u=\operatorname{cosec}x\) and \(dv=\operatorname{cosec}^2x\,dx\), we get \(J=-\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x-\int\operatorname{cosec}x\cot^2x\,dx\).

Using \(\cot^2x=\operatorname{cosec}^2x-1\), we get \(J=-\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x-J+\int\operatorname{cosec}x\,dx\).

Therefore, \(2J=-\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x+\ln\left|\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right|\).

Hence \(J=-\dfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x+\dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left|\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right|+C\).

Substituting in the equation for \(I\), we get \(I=-\dfrac{1}{4}\operatorname{cosec}^3x\cot x-\dfrac{3}{8}\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x+\dfrac{3}{8}\ln\left|\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right|+C\).

Factoring the first two terms, \(I=-\dfrac{1}{4}\cot x\operatorname{cosec}x\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2x+\dfrac{3}{2}\right)+\dfrac{3}{8}\ln\left|\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right|+C\).

Thus \(\alpha=-\dfrac{1}{4}\) and \(\beta=\dfrac{3}{8}\).

Therefore, \(8(\alpha+\beta)=8\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}+\dfrac{3}{8}\right)=1\).

Let y=y(x) be the solution of the differential equation (x+y+2)2dx=dy,y(0)=-2. Let the maximum and minimum values of the function y=y(x) in 0,π3 be α and β, respectively. If (3α+π)2+β2=γ+δ3,γ,δ∈Z, then γ+δ equals _________ .

questions.explanation:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=(x+y+2)^2\)

Let \(z=x+y+2\).

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dz}{dx}=1+\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1+z^2\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dz}{1+z^2}=dx\)

\(\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}z=x+C\)

Using \(y(0)=-2\), we get \(z(0)=0\).

\(\Rightarrow C=0\)

\(\Rightarrow z=\tan x\)

\(\Rightarrow y=\tan x-x-2\)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\sec^2x-1=\tan^2x\geq0\) for \(x\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right]\).

The function is increasing on the given interval.

\(\beta=y(0)=-2\)

\(\alpha=y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\sqrt3-\dfrac{\pi}{3}-2\)

\(\Rightarrow 3\alpha+\pi=3\sqrt3-6\)

\(\Rightarrow (3\alpha+\pi)^2+\beta^2=(3\sqrt3-6)^2+4\)

\(\Rightarrow (3\alpha+\pi)^2+\beta^2=63-36\sqrt3+4\)

\(\Rightarrow (3\alpha+\pi)^2+\beta^2=67-36\sqrt3\)

Comparing with \(\gamma+\delta\sqrt3\), we get \(\gamma=67,\ \delta=-36\)

\(\Rightarrow \gamma+\delta=31\)

The required value is \(31\).

The line \(L\) passes through \(P=(1,2,1)\) and has direction vector

\(\vec d=(2,1,-1)-(1,2,1)=(1,-1,-2)\)

Let \(A=(2,2,2)\) and let \(H=P+t\vec d\) be the foot of the perpendicular from \(A\) to \(L\).

\(\because AH\perp\vec d\), \((A-H)\cdot\vec d=0\)

\(\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{(A-P)\cdot\vec d}{|\vec d|^2}\)

\(\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{(1,0,1)\cdot(1,-1,-2)}{1+1+4}=-\dfrac16\)

\(\Rightarrow H=\left(\dfrac56,\dfrac{13}{6},\dfrac43\right)\)

If \(A'=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\) is the mirror image, then

\(A'=2H-A\)

\(\Rightarrow A'=\left(-\dfrac13,\dfrac73,\dfrac23\right)\)

\(\alpha+\beta+6\gamma=-\dfrac13+\dfrac73+6\left(\dfrac23\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow \alpha+\beta+6\gamma=6\)

The required value is \(6\).
